sub_graphs.name: Transaction Gas Limit Cap Constant
sub_graphs.description: Defines the protocol-level constant MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT = 16,777,216 (2^24). This is the hard upper bound on the gasLimit field of any individual transaction, independent of the block gas limit.

invariants.text: MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT = 2^24 = 16,777,216. This constant is fixed at the protocol level and does not change with block gas limit adjustments.

The transaction gas cap is strictly independent of the block gas limit. The block gas limit may exceed 16,777,216, but no single transaction within that block may have a gasLimit exceeding 16,777,216.

state_variables.name: MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT
state_variables.description: Protocol-level constant defining the maximum gas any single transaction may specify. Equal to 2^24.

security_notes: The power-of-two boundary (2^24) simplifies implementation and bitwise comparisons in client code.

sub_graphs.name: Transaction Pool Validation Gate
sub_graphs.description: Enforces the gas limit cap at the transaction pool (mempool) ingestion layer. Transactions with gasLimit > MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT are rejected before entering the txpool.

invariants.text: No transaction in the txpool shall have a gasLimit exceeding MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT (16,777,216).

functions.description: During transaction validation at txpool ingestion, if tx.gasLimit > 16,777,216, the transaction is invalidated and not included in the txpool. Returns error code MAX_GAS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

pre_conditions.text: A transaction is submitted to the node for inclusion in the txpool.

post_conditions.text: If tx.gasLimit > 16,777,216, the transaction is rejected with MAX_GAS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and does NOT enter the txpool.
If tx.gasLimit <= 16,777,216, the transaction proceeds through remaining validation checks (signature, nonce, balance, etc.).

state_transitions.description: Transactions exceeding the gas cap are immediately rejected at the txpool validation layer, preventing propagation through the network.
Transactions within the gas cap pass this validation gate and continue to subsequent txpool admission checks.

security_notes: This is the first line of defense: prevents over-gas transactions from consuming txpool resources or being gossiped to peers.
Mitigates DoS at the mempool level by rejecting oversized transactions before they consume validation resources.

sub_graphs.name: Block-Level Transaction Gas Limit Validation
sub_graphs.description: Enforces the gas limit cap at the block validation layer. Any block containing a transaction with gasLimit > MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT is deemed invalid and rejected during consensus processing.

invariants.text: For every transaction tx in a valid block: tx.gasLimit <= MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT (16,777,216).
A block is invalid if ANY transaction within it has gasLimit > 16,777,216, regardless of the block's total gas limit.

functions.description: During block validation (before transaction processing/execution), iterates over all transactions in the block. If any transaction has gasLimit > 16,777,216, the entire block is rejected as invalid.
functions.pseudo_logic: for tx in block.transactions: if tx.gasLimit > MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT: return (false, 'INVALID_BLOCK: transaction gas limit exceeds cap')

pre_conditions.text: A block is received by a node for validation (either from the network or produced locally).

post_conditions.text: If any tx in block has gasLimit > 16,777,216, the block is rejected as invalid and not appended to the chain.
If all transactions have gasLimit <= 16,777,216, the block proceeds to further consensus validation steps.

state_transitions.trigger: Any tx in block has gasLimit > MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT
state_transitions.description: Blocks containing any over-gas-cap transaction are entirely rejected during the pre-execution validation phase.

state_transitions.to_state: Block passes gas cap validation (proceeds to execution)
state_transitions.trigger: All tx in block have gasLimit <= MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT
state_transitions.description: Blocks where all transactions respect the gas cap pass this validation gate.

security_notes: This is the consensus-critical enforcement layer. Even if a txpool validation is bypassed (e.g., by a malicious block producer), this check ensures invalid blocks are rejected by all honest nodes.
Provides block verification stability by ensuring no single transaction can dominate block processing time.
Reduces worst-case block verification times, improving network synchronization and decentralization.

sub_graphs.name: DoS Attack Surface Reduction
sub_graphs.description: The gas cap directly mitigates denial-of-service vectors where a single high-gas transaction could consume the entire block gas limit, causing uneven load distribution and impacting network stability.

invariants.text: No single transaction can consume more than 16,777,216 / block_gas_limit fraction of a block's capacity (approximately 50% of a 30M gas block, or ~40% of a 40M gas block).
Every valid block must contain room for at least floor(block_gas_limit / MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT) - 1 additional minimum-gas transactions, ensuring no single transaction can monopolize block space.

security_notes: A single transaction consuming the entire block gas limit was previously a viable DoS vector. This EIP ensures at minimum ~2 transactions per block at typical 30-40M gas limits.
Reduces state bloat risk: high-gas transactions often correlate with large state changes, and capping gas limits the maximum state delta per transaction.
Improves fairness of gas allocation across transactions within a block.
Critical for scaling the block gas limit upward: as the gas limit increases, the cap ensures the worst-case per-transaction cost remains bounded.

sub_graphs.name: Backward Compatibility Constraints
sub_graphs.description: Documents the backward compatibility implications of the gas cap. This is a hard fork change: transactions with gasLimit > 16,777,216 that were previously valid will be rejected after activation.

invariants.text: All transactions with gasLimit <= 16,777,216 remain fully valid and unaffected by this change.
After activation, transactions with gasLimit > 16,777,216 are universally invalid across all compliant nodes.

state_transitions.trigger: Hard fork activation at designated block/timestamp
state_transitions.description: After activation, the protocol transitions from no per-transaction gas cap to enforcing a 16,777,216 gas maximum per transaction. Transactions exceeding the cap that may have been valid before become invalid.

security_notes: Empirical analysis shows minimal impact: most transactions today fall well below the 16,777,216 gas cap.
Complex contract deployments and certain batch operations that exceed the cap will need to be re-architected into multiple transactions.
Tooling and dApp frontends need minor updates to enforce the cap when constructing transactions.

sub_graphs.name: Client Implementation Requirements
sub_graphs.description: Specifies the changes required in Ethereum client implementations to enforce the transaction gas limit cap at both the transaction pool and block validation layers.

invariants.text: The GAS_LIMIT parameter for transactions is capped at 16,777,216 in all compliant client implementations.

functions.description: Utility function in client implementations to check whether a transaction's gas limit is within the protocol cap.

state_variables.name: MAX_TRANSACTION_GAS_LIMIT
state_variables.description: Protocol constant to be defined in client configuration, used in both txpool validation and block validation code paths.

data_structures.name: TransactionValidationError
data_structures.description: Error type/code returned when a transaction exceeds the gas cap.

fields.name: message
fields.value: Transaction gas limit exceeds maximum allowed (16,777,216)

security_notes: Both txpool and block validation must independently enforce the cap for defense-in-depth.
The cap check must occur before transaction execution to prevent resource exhaustion.

sub_graphs.title: EIP-7883: ModExp Gas Cost Increase
sub_graphs.description: Modifies the ModExp precompile pricing algorithm from EIP-2565: increases minimum gas from 200 to 500, triples general cost, and doubles the cost for exponents larger than 32 bytes.

sub_graphs.name: ModExp Gas Cost Calculation (Top-Level)
sub_graphs.description: The top-level gas cost function for the ModExp precompile at address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000005. Computes the final gas cost as max(500, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count)). This replaces the EIP-2565 formula max(200, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count / 3)), raising the minimum from 200 to 500 and tripling the general cost by removing the division by 3.

invariants.text: The gas cost MUST always be at least 500 (increased from the EIP-2565 minimum of 200).
The gas cost MUST equal max(500, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count)) where multiplication_complexity and iteration_count are computed by their respective sub-functions.
The gas cost MUST be a non-negative integer (result of floor applied to non-negative product, then max with 500).
For any given inputs, the EIP-7883 gas cost MUST be >= the EIP-2565 gas cost for the same inputs (since the minimum is higher and the divisor of 3 was removed).

pre_conditions.text: base_length, modulus_length, and exponent_length MUST be non-negative integers derived from the input to the ModExp precompile call.
exponent MUST be the numeric value of the exponent input (or the first 256 bits if exponent_length > 32).
This EIP MUST be active (i.e., the fork activating EIP-7883 has occurred).

post_conditions.text: The returned gas cost is an integer >= 500.
The caller is charged exactly the returned gas amount for the ModExp precompile invocation.

functions.name: calculate_gas_cost

parameters.name: base_length
parameters.description: The byte-length of the base input to the ModExp precompile.

parameters.name: modulus_length
parameters.description: The byte-length of the modulus input to the ModExp precompile.

parameters.name: exponent_length
parameters.description: The byte-length of the exponent input to the ModExp precompile.

parameters.name: exponent
parameters.description: The numeric value of the exponent (or the first 256 bits if exponent_length > 32).

functions.description: Computes the gas cost for a ModExp precompile call as max(500, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count)). Changed from EIP-2565 which used max(200, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count / 3)).
modifications: [Changed in EIP-7883] Minimum gas raised from 200 to 500
[Changed in EIP-7883] Division by 3 removed, tripling the general cost

sub_graphs.name: Multiplication Complexity Calculation
sub_graphs.description: Computes the multiplication complexity factor based on the byte-lengths of the base and modulus inputs. In EIP-7883, a minimum complexity of 16 is introduced (equivalent to 4 words squared times 1, representing a 32-byte input baseline). For inputs exceeding 32 bytes, the complexity is doubled compared to EIP-2565 (2 * words^2 instead of words^2).

invariants.text: The multiplication_complexity MUST always be at least 16 (representing the baseline cost for inputs up to 32 bytes).
For max(base_length, modulus_length) <= 32, multiplication_complexity MUST equal 16.
For max(base_length, modulus_length) > 32, multiplication_complexity MUST equal 2 * ceil(max_length / 8)^2.
The multiplication_complexity is symmetric with respect to base_length and modulus_length (only the max of the two matters).

pre_conditions.text: base_length and modulus_length MUST be non-negative integers.

post_conditions.text: The returned multiplication_complexity is a positive integer >= 16.

functions.name: calculate_multiplication_complexity

parameters.name: base_length
parameters.description: The byte-length of the base input.

parameters.name: modulus_length
parameters.description: The byte-length of the modulus input.

functions.description: Computes multiplication complexity. Sets max_length = max(base_length, modulus_length), words = ceil(max_length / 8). Returns 16 if max_length <= 32, otherwise returns 2 * words^2.
modifications: [Changed in EIP-7883] Baseline complexity of 16 introduced for inputs <= 32 bytes
[Changed in EIP-7883] For inputs > 32 bytes, complexity doubled from words^2 to 2 * words^2

state_variables.name: max_length
state_variables.description: The maximum of base_length and modulus_length; determines which branch of the complexity formula is used.

state_variables.name: words
state_variables.description: The number of 8-byte words needed to represent the larger of base or modulus: ceil(max_length / 8).

state_variables.name: multiplication_complexity
state_variables.description: The computed complexity factor. Initialized to 16, then conditionally set to 2 * words^2 if max_length > 32.

sub_graphs.name: Iteration Count Calculation
sub_graphs.description: Computes the iteration count based on the exponent's byte-length and value. For exponents larger than 32 bytes, EIP-7883 doubles the multiplier from 8 to 16 compared to EIP-2565.

invariants.text: The iteration_count MUST always be at least 1.
If exponent_length <= 32 and exponent == 0, then iteration_count MUST be 1.
If exponent_length <= 32 and exponent > 0, then iteration_count MUST equal exponent.bit_length() - 1 (or 1 if that value is 0).
If exponent_length > 32, then iteration_count MUST equal (16 * (exponent_length - 32)) + ((exponent & (2^256 - 1)).bit_length() - 1), with a minimum of 1.

pre_conditions.text: exponent_length MUST be a non-negative integer.
exponent MUST be a non-negative integer representing the exponent value (or the first 256 bits thereof if exponent_length > 32).

post_conditions.text: The returned iteration_count is a positive integer >= 1.

functions.name: calculate_iteration_count

parameters.name: exponent_length
parameters.description: The byte-length of the exponent input.

parameters.name: exponent
parameters.description: The numeric value of the exponent (or the first 256 bits if exponent_length > 32).

functions.description: Computes the iteration count. For exponent_length <= 32: returns 0 if exponent is 0, else exponent.bit_length() - 1. For exponent_length > 32: returns (16 * (exponent_length - 32)) + ((exponent & (2^256 - 1)).bit_length() - 1). Clamped to minimum of 1.
modifications: [Changed in EIP-7883] Large exponent multiplier doubled from 8 to 16 for exponent_length > 32

state_variables.name: iteration_count
state_variables.description: The computed number of iterations. Clamped to a minimum of 1.

sub_graphs.name: Pricing Change: Minimum and General Cost Increase
sub_graphs.description: The minimum gas cost is raised from 200 to 500, and the general cost is tripled by removing the division by 3.

invariants.text: The minimum gas cost for any ModExp call MUST be 500 (previously 200 under EIP-2565).
The general cost formula MUST NOT include a division by 3.
For the most common historical ModExp usage patterns (~99.69% of calls), the gas cost increase MUST be between 150% and 200%.

state_transitions.text: Gas cost formula transitions from max(200, floor(mc * ic / 3)) to max(500, floor(mc * ic)).

sub_graphs.name: Pricing Change: Large Exponent Cost Doubling
sub_graphs.description: For exponents larger than 32 bytes, the iteration count multiplier is increased from 8 to 16, doubling the cost contribution of large exponents.

invariants.text: For exponent_length > 32, the large-exponent component of iteration_count MUST use a multiplier of 16 (previously 8).
For exponent_length <= 32, the iteration_count calculation is unchanged from EIP-2565.

state_transitions.text: Large exponent iteration count formula transitions from 8 * (exponent_length - 32) to 16 * (exponent_length - 32).

sub_graphs.name: Pricing Change: Minimum Base/Modulus Complexity and Large Input Doubling
sub_graphs.description: A minimum multiplication complexity of 16 is introduced, and complexity is doubled (2 * words^2 instead of words^2) for inputs exceeding 32 bytes.

invariants.text: The multiplication_complexity MUST be at least 16 regardless of input sizes.
For max(base_length, modulus_length) > 32, multiplication_complexity MUST be 2 * words^2 (previously words^2).

state_transitions.text: Multiplication complexity formula transitions from words^2 to 16 if <= 32 bytes, else 2 * words^2.

sub_graphs.name: ModExp Precompile Target Address
sub_graphs.description: The ModExp precompile resides at address 0x05. Only gas metering is modified; arithmetic behavior is unchanged.

invariants.text: The ModExp precompile address MUST remain 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000005.
The ModExp precompile's arithmetic behavior and input/output format MUST remain unchanged from EIP-198/EIP-2565.
Only the gas cost calculation is modified; no changes to the underlying modular exponentiation algorithm.

pre_conditions.text: A CALL, STATICCALL, or DELEGATECALL is made to address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000005.

post_conditions.text: Gas is metered according to the EIP-7883 formula (if fork is active) before executing the modular exponentiation.

sub_graphs.name: Backwards Compatibility and Security Considerations
sub_graphs.description: No new functionality is introduced and no existing operations become cheaper. The primary risk is potential overpricing of certain ModExp scenarios.

invariants.text: No new operations or opcodes are introduced; only the cost of the existing ModExp precompile is changed.
No existing operations become cheaper under EIP-7883.
Existing ModExp test vectors remain valid for arithmetic correctness; only expected gas values change.
